The rise of digital assets has been driven via anti-fragility.

Frontier Math breakthroughs and quantum computing are perceived to be an existential threat. These threats do have merit. But I am confident we will navigate them at large and there will be no disastrous event. 

The concept of anti-fragility means something benefits from volatility and is not crushed by it. Over time the system becomes stronger. I view any future changes to the cryptography underpinning public blockchains as this. 

If I were to identify the most fragile point for blockchains it's not the underlying cryptography. Its the fact malicious state changes are irreversible and are physic like events. You cannot reverse time after a collision has occurred. Finality is the collision. 

I am fully pro having some form of policy engine imbedded directly at the block builder/sequencer level where malicious transactions cannot be mined. This to me remains a far significant threat vector than frontier math AI breakthroughs.

Physical AI + Humanoids are the next progression of AI.

$NVDA CES 2025 projections and Elon's prediction on $TSLA + 1 Billion humanoids in the next decade, seems to be speeding up. 

New statement from Unitree CEO after testing GPT-6 on their humanoid program was that:

- In August, before GPT-6's release, Wang said the industry could take two to three years at its fastest pace, or as long as a decade, to reach its "ChatGPT moment"

- Now, OpenAI's GPT-6 model prompted expectations that a breakthrough could happen "within 1 or 2 years"

- He defined that moment as robots being able to complete around 80 per cent of tasks in 80 per cent of unfamiliar environments using voice or text commands.

- "It's possible that, say, a GPT-7 model released next year could directly crack the problems of embodied intelligence"

- "The whole embodied intelligence industry has been shaken up after the release of GPT-6"

Just looking at some benchmarks on robotic hand manipulation, "On the bowl task Astra placed the block in 19 of 20 trials, against Fable 5.1's 8 of 20".

But for the puzzle task "Astra completed the insertion 2 times in 20 against Fable 5.1's 2 in 20"".. so we're getting there. 

But going from 2-3 years (potentially to a decade), and compressing that down to 1 or 2 years (to achieve 80%+ of tasks in unfamiliar environemnts) is a significant change in outlook.

When I first got into crypto from a technical perspective there were many incredibly interesting esoteric ideas that were truly frontier ideas.

I remember pre 2020 prediction markets were first called truth markets. But on-chain infrastructure had not caught up yet to make the idea go mainstream.

It seems we are entering a phase now where these esoteric ideas may become front and centre. Few ideas being the following:

[1] Proof of Humanity: This to me now seems tautological and digital interactions seek trust now more than ever. Adversarial actors and AI passing the Turing test for both audio/visual interactions seems sufficient enough to have a PoH everywhere (emails, online calls, socials).

[2] PQ Cryptography: Emerging threat vectors from Quantum computing and breakthroughs in frontier Math that may expose weaknesses in traditional ECDSA. The ability to attain a private key from an exposed public key. Explains the rise of ZEC as a hedge to threat vectors to Bitcoin core and it's ossification leading to a delayed response.

[3] Private Inference: Concerns arising from frontier labs distilling their own users. Corporations are seeking hosting their own models ands training them on their own operations. Coinbase recently announced they trained their own model for a specific business function. I do think private inference of frontier intelligence protecting user thought and intellectual property will have a strong attractor over time.

These ideas were early and have existed for some time but the world they were building for did not exist. It's difficult to see where we are going and the end state but I now think these ideas will begin to see wider adoption.

So spent some more time to look at more DBS conference material: 

- "Two semiconductor giants, $AVGO and $INTC, both stated that breakthroughs in AI will keep demand for chip investment elevated for at least another 2 years. As current supply is insufficient to meet market demand."

- "Current chip production capacity is already far from sufficient to meet demand, and $AVGO CEO expects the shortage to become even more severe in the future." (HKEJ) 

- "Regarding OpenAI, Hock Tan stated that the market had misinterpreted the company because its underlying fundamentals remained strong.

He argued that investors who sell based on a single short-term data point [$50B ARR] are "essentially no different from people gambling in a casino." (eg. Hong Kong Economic Journal):

- Commenting on investors' disappointment in OpenAI’s latest revenue forecast: "by itself, not that bad" on their $50B ARR. (Business Times)

And connected investors' disappointment to a failure to understand the business and excessive expectations like a casino. 

- Tan rejected the proposition that OpenAI was overvalued. It quotes him saying:

"It’s almost like they are in a casino gambling" in regards to investors' unrealistic expectations and lack of understanding on OpenAI.

- Hock Tan if OpenAI and Anthropic achieve widespread market adoption: their attractiveness would substantially strengthen their bargaining power when raising capital. 

But cautioned elevated global interest rates could make capital requirements a constraint for future growth.

- The real driver, he said, is whether frontier AI companies can create models that generate enough value and returns to justify the buildout. (which is fair)

- Most companies are wasting money on tokens. He also warned that most companies just waste money spending tokens like kids in a video arcade.

This part was the most badly worded by Hock Tan given he's running $AVGO. 

But Western media commentary narrowed this down to:
- "Shortage of capital now, AI Investors are gamblers". 

In the conference, Broadcom's CEO was actually defending frontier lab valuations and giving cautiously bullish statements about AI infrastructure demand. 

While citing rising interest rates as a potential constraint that larger revenue or adoption could overcome. 

Cherry picking quotes out of context disorts the actual messaging. 

TLDR:

- Large and elevated AI semi demand, semi supply insufficient to meet market demand. At least another 2 years of elevated spend

- OpenAI valuations defensible, people who sell based on extreme expectations for the company are like casino gamblers. 

- Tan stated markets had misinterpreted OpenAI's ARR because its underlying fundamentals remained strong.

-  Frontier labs if they achieve widespread adoption / revenue would strengthen capital raising, which overpower headwinds from raising interest rates. 

Lot of $AVGO CEO remarks looks heavily nuanced, which Western media coverage distored.
